---
name: story-to-spec
description: Convert US-01, US-02, or US-03 from the multi-country insurance technical assessment into a testable, source-grounded specification before implementation.
---

# Story to Specification

## Inputs
- Original assessment: `requirements/technical-assessment.pdf`.
- User-story identifier and source text.
- `AGENTS.md` and any applicable approved ADRs.

## Repeatable procedure
1. Extract source-stated story, business rules and acceptance scenarios with page references.
2. Build a requirement-to-observable-behavior-to-test traceability table.
3. Define proposed Strapi/Angular contracts and specify loading, empty, invalid and failure states.
4. Identify missing decisions. Label each as **Question** or **Proposal**, never as a verbatim source requirement.
5. Write verifiable Given/When/Then cases covering both countries when applicable.
6. Save to `spec/US-XX.md` with status **Pending human approval**.
7. Request a human decision. If rejected, document feedback and revise the spec, retaining the review record.

## Expected result
A reviewable, testable and traceable specification. No application implementation and no self-approval.
spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md:12:| ADR-005 persists only the country and quote number. The approved confirmation shows the reference. | Preserve a frozen, masked review of the completed Details, chosen plan and final price with the receipt. Restore the same review after reload even if Strapi content changes. This requires revising the minimal receipt storage decision. |
spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md:20:| AC-US03-R02 | Confirmation displays the approval, quote reference and read-only Details and plan/final price as captured at approval. The document remains masked. Changes to live form labels, plan prices or availability do not alter a completed quote. | In both countries, verify the approved projection and masked value, then reload after a changed or unavailable catalog and compare the receipt and projection. |
spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md:26:- Propose persisting only the frozen display projection needed for the receipt, including the already masked document value. Keep the existing country- and tab-scoped boundary. Do not derive historical values from mutable drafts or live content after approval.
docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md:23:| `purpose` | Optional semantic marker, unique per reserved role. A usable form contains one required `dateOfBirth` date with `minimumAge` 18 and one required `vehicleYear` number with `vehicleYearRange`. `identityDocument` and `licensePlate` markers, when present, use text fields. This enables masking and pricing without relying on visible labels. |
docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md:43:Use Typed Reactive Forms with `FormRecord<FormControl<FieldValue | null>>` and a discriminated field/view model. Keys are dynamic and the control's static value type is the common union. Narrow by the decoded field kind and normalize at the control adapter and output boundaries. Use actual typed number and Boolean values, preserve meaningful empty or unset state, and track rendered elements by stable ID. Stay with native inputs and selects and an unset, non-selectable required-select placeholder. The first invalid field gets focus on an unsuccessful Continue. Keep Continue available after the configuration is ready, with application validation controlling progress and custom messages. Use native form semantics with an explicit Angular submit handler and no browser validation bubbles masking configured messages. On blur expose that field's message, on change reevaluate touched fields, and on submit expose all applicable errors. Associate visible errors and help through stable DOM IDs and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` when showing an error. Use concise status announcements for loading and retry, and avoid announcing the same validation error twice when moving focus. [Angular typed forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/typed-forms)
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:23:After the live attempt passes its final eligibility check, use the existing review projector to capture ordered label and display-value rows, including the already masked identity document. Capture the chosen plan's displayed name and validated final `{ amountMinor, currency }` at the same transition. Generate the existing opaque quote reference once and commit the immutable receipt as one snapshot. Copy display values out of the editable state. Restore and display the snapshot with the existing country money formatter. A published change, removal or outage cannot alter it. Treat values as plain text in both visible and accessible output.
docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md:54:- **AC-US03-R02** — In each country, compare the masked captured review, amount and reference after changed or unavailable Strapi content. Test the worst-case valid projection against the codec, and reject corrupted and wrong-country envelopes. Verify that failed writes retain the full review in memory.
docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md:33:Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.
docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md:22:- **US-03** derives the review from current country fields and masks the identity document in presentation. Use stable field purpose metadata to locate the document independently of its label. Bind consent to the current terms revision and quote snapshot. Proposed duplicate protection is an atomic attempt transition in the same store, from eligible to processing before the asynchronous simulation starts. Only the matching attempt can settle, repeat clicks do not enqueue, success keeps one confirmation number for that completed quote, and a reported failure may retry. The US-03 spec and checkpoint will decide how reload handles a persisted processing attempt and completed receipt. No real gateway, card data or global idempotency service is implied.
spec/US-03.md:22:- Partially mask the identity document in the summary using the same rule in both countries, including its accessible presentation.
spec/US-03.md:34:- Use each current form field's configured label and stable purpose metadata. Locate the document by `identityDocument` purpose, not by its label. Exclude values removed from the current form configuration.
spec/US-03.md:49:| US03-SR-03 | Partially mask the document number in the summary. | Page 8, business rules |
spec/US-03.md:74:### AC-US03-02 — Shared document masking rule
spec/US-03.md:76:**Given** the current form has a field with `identityDocument` purpose and it has a value
spec/US-03.md:80:**Then** the same masking rule applies in Colombia and Chile, revealing at most the last four alphanumeric characters for longer values
spec/US-03.md:84:**And** a one-character value is fully masked
spec/US-03.md:207:| T-US03-02 | Component/accessibility | Verify the shared masking rule in both countries for long, two-to-four-character and one-character values, and verify the full value does not appear in visual or accessible summary output. |
spec/US-03.md:221:- ADR-003 already specifies identity-document masking by stable `identityDocument` purpose, consent bound to the current terms revision and quote snapshot, an atomic processing state for duplicate protection, one confirmation number per successful quote and retry after reported failure. This draft resolves its reserved reload behavior: interrupted payment is retryable and completed receipt is preserved with duplicate payment blocked.
spec/US-03.md:223:- The current Angular wizard has a `/summary` handoff after Details and plan revalidation. Summary is still a placeholder. The shared form contract contains `identityDocument` purpose metadata and the plan contract contains final `basePrice` data. The current Strapi content projection serves forms and plans; it has no terms content or terms read contract. No Summary terms or payment behavior exists yet.
spec/US-03.md:230:| Q-US03-01 | Resolved by owner clarification | Apply the same masking rule in both countries: reveal at most the final four alphanumeric characters for longer values; for two-to-four-character values, reveal only the last character; fully mask a one-character value; preserve separators. |
spec/US-03.md:237:- **Always:** Use the active country's current quote state; show a partially masked identity document; require current terms consent; keep payment simulated; retain quote information through a reported failure; and prevent duplicate attempts.
- The project owner separately authorized two commits. The orchestrator used `git-workflow-and-versioning` to group the terminal implementation and its previously uncommitted US-03 dependencies with their regression tests, and to group QA, review, workflow and final approval evidence in a separate documentation commit.

## Skill selection and controls

The project-specific `story-to-spec` skill defines the insurance assessment source and specification format. Other installed skills are third-party workflow or technical guidance. Select skills by stage and task as listed in `AGENTS.md`. Conditional skills are loaded only when the work warrants them. Project instructions and assessment requirements take precedence over conflicting skill guidance. Skills do not bypass security restrictions or human approval checkpoints. Record skills actually used in execution evidence and keep this proposed flow distinct from completed work.

## Git conventions and authorization

Use English Conventional Commit messages in `<type>(<optional-scope>): <description>` format, with focused atomic changes. Suggest a commit message when work is ready. Staging, committing, pushing, merging, branch creation or deletion, history rewriting, and destructive Git actions each require explicit human authorization for that operation. Approval of a specification or code does not grant Git authorization. Read-only Git inspection is allowed. Never place credentials, secrets, personal data, or sensitive information in commits or logs.

## Model allocation and usage

Keep the configured model and effort assignments from `docs/agent-model-policy.md`. Choose the least number of agents and skills needed for a task. Avoid loading all skills or invoking agents without a concrete independent responsibility. The project targets a ChatGPT Plus subscription, so use focused prompts, narrow source reads, sequential checkpoints, and only the context needed for each stage. Do not claim a subscription allowance, cost, or usage outcome that has not been verified.

## Required retrospective (complete with authentic experience)

## Traceability and verification levels

Maintain `User Story → spec/US-XX.md → applicable approved ADRs → approved design (when requested) → implementation → stable test case IDs → reports/qa/US-XX-qa-report.md → reviews/US-XX-review.md → finding resolution evidence → human approval`. Reference repository paths and actual evidence. Reuse approved ADRs when they cover the story. Story reports cover the current story only. Complete quote-flow and cross-country verification are project-level checks before final delivery, not prerequisites for each story when later stories are pending.

### How would this flow change for a five-developer team?
To be completed after applying the process. Consider ownership boundaries, review queues, parallel safe tasks, and shared quality gates.

### What did not work as expected, and what changed?
To be completed using actual incidents only. Never invent a process failure.

### Where did we deliberately avoid using AI, and why?
To be completed using actual human checkpoints and decisions.
# Original Agent Session Evidence

The assessment requires unedited logs or exports of agent sessions. Do not replace them with summaries or invented transcripts.

For the Codex desktop app:
1. Preserve original chats and subagent threads in the app; inspect activity to verify which roles actually ran.
2. Use a native export or copy mechanism only if the installed app actually provides one. Do **not** assume the CLI-only `/export` command is available in the app.
3. If needed and supported by your environment, locate Codex's locally persisted session records and copy the relevant originals unchanged into `logs/` (the exact location and format can vary by version/platform).
4. Record the source, original timestamp, actual model/effort, session or thread identifier, and related story/commit in `FLOW.md` or a separate index. Keep notes separate from raw exports.
5. Before publishing, inspect originals for credentials, personal data, tokens and other sensitive information. Avoid putting such data in prompts in the first place; do not publish unsafe originals.
6. If no safe, unedited export is possible, disclose that limitation rather than manufacturing evidence.

No agent session has been executed by this starter package.

---
name: git-workflow-and-versioning
description: Structures git workflow practices. Use when making any code change. Use when committing, branching, resolving conflicts, splitting uncommitted work in a messy working tree into clean atomic commits, opening or reviewing a pull request (PR), pushing to a remote, or when you need to organize work across multiple parallel streams. Use when cutting a release, choosing a semantic version bump, tagging, or writing a changelog. Use when asked to write a commit message or a changelog entry for a change, or to split a change into commits, even when the diff is pasted inline and the message seems easy to write from it.
---

# Git Workflow and Versioning

## Overview

Git is your safety net. Treat commits as save points, branches as sandboxes, and history as documentation. With AI agents generating code at high speed, disciplined version control is the mechanism that keeps changes manageable, reviewable, and reversible.

## When to Use

Always. Every code change flows through git.

## Core Principles

### Trunk-Based Development (Recommended)

Keep `main` always deployable. Work in short-lived feature branches that merge back within 1-3 days. Long-lived development branches are hidden costs — they diverge, create merge conflicts, and delay integration. DORA research consistently shows trunk-based development correlates with high-performing engineering teams.

```
main ──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──  (always deployable)
        ╲      ╱  ╲    ╱
         ●──●─╱    ●──╱    ← short-lived feature branches (1-3 days)
```

This is the recommended default. Teams using gitflow or long-lived branches can adapt the principles (atomic commits, small changes, descriptive messages) to their branching model — the commit discipline matters more than the specific branching strategy.

- **Dev branches are costs.** Every day a branch lives, it accumulates merge risk.
- **Release branches are acceptable.** When you need to stabilize a release while main moves forward.
- **Feature flags > long branches.** Prefer deploying incomplete work behind flags rather than keeping it on a branch for weeks.

### 1. Commit Early, Commit Often

Each successful increment gets its own commit. Don't accumulate large uncommitted changes.

```
Work pattern:
  Implement slice → Test → Verify → Commit → Next slice

Not this:
  Implement everything → Hope it works → Giant commit
```

Use when committing, branching, resolving conflicts, splitting uncommitted work in a messy working tree into clean atomic commits, opening or reviewing a pull request (PR), pushing to a remote, or when you need to organize work across multiple parallel streams. Use when cutting a release, choosing a semantic version bump, tagging, or writing a changelog. Use when asked to write a commit message or a changelog entry for a change, or to split a change into commits, even when the diff is pasted inline and the message seems easy to write from it.
---

# Git Workflow and Versioning

## Overview

Git is your safety net. Treat commits as save points, branches as sandboxes, and history as documentation. With AI agents generating code at high speed, disciplined version control is the mechanism that keeps changes manageable, reviewable, and reversible.

## When to Use

Always. Every code change flows through git.

## Core Principles

### Trunk-Based Development (Recommended)

Keep `main` always deployable. Work in short-lived feature branches that merge back within 1-3 days. Long-lived development branches are hidden costs — they diverge, create merge conflicts, and delay integration. DORA research consistently shows trunk-based development correlates with high-performing engineering teams.

```
main ──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──  (always deployable)
        ╲      ╱  ╲    ╱
         ●──●─╱    ●──╱    ← short-lived feature branches (1-3 days)
```

This is the recommended default. Teams using gitflow or long-lived branches can adapt the principles (atomic commits, small changes, descriptive messages) to their branching model — the commit discipline matters more than the specific branching strategy.

- **Dev branches are costs.** Every day a branch lives, it accumulates merge risk.
- **Release branches are acceptable.** When you need to stabilize a release while main moves forward.
- **Feature flags > long branches.** Prefer deploying incomplete work behind flags rather than keeping it on a branch for weeks.

### 1. Commit Early, Commit Often

Each successful increment gets its own commit. Don't accumulate large uncommitted changes.

```
Work pattern:
  Implement slice → Test → Verify → Commit → Next slice

Not this:
  Implement everything → Hope it works → Giant commit
```

# US-03 — Identity document masking correction

**Status:** Pending human approval

**Source:** [Technical assessment](../requirements/technical-assessment.pdf), page 8, business rules

**Related stories:** US-01 — Policyholder and vehicle data form; US-03 — Summary and payment

**Related approved decisions:** [ADR-002](../docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), [ADR-005](../docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), and [terminal quote amendment](../docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md)

## Problem and objective

The assessment requires the document number to be partially masked in the quote summary. The current approved contract treats the `identityDocument` purpose as optional, and Summary locates the document using that purpose. A published configuration can keep a document-number field but remove its purpose. That configuration remains valid while Summary displays the full value. This correction makes the masking invariant survive supported form publication and completed-quote restoration.

## Scope

- Require each usable country form to identify its policyholder document using exactly one `identityDocument` purpose marker on a required text field.
- Keep the marker independent of editable labels, field order, and Strapi component IDs.
- Reject a published form with no identity-document field, multiple such markers, or a marker on an incompatible field. Follow the existing atomic configuration failure and retry behavior. Preserve the user's draft without rendering a partially refreshed form.
- Apply the approved masking rule to all visible and accessible Summary output and to any newly captured terminal quote review.
- Define safe behavior for already stored drafts and terminal receipts made under the previously optional-purpose contract before changing production code.

The source requires a partially masked document number. Requiring a stable contract marker and rejecting malformed content are proposed implementation decisions, not additional wording from the assessment.

## Proposed acceptance criteria

### AC-US03-M01 — A usable form identifies its document field

**Given** a published country form is decoded

**When** it contains exactly one required text field with `identityDocument` purpose

**Then** the form is usable and Summary locates the document by purpose regardless of its label or order.

**And** Colombia and Chile use the same contract rule.

### AC-US03-M02 — Invalid identity metadata fails closed

**Given** a published form has a missing, duplicate, or incompatible `identityDocument` purpose

**When** the form is loaded or refreshed

**Then** the whole form snapshot is rejected and the established recoverable error and retry state is shown

**And** the app does not render the affected document field or its raw value in Summary

**And** a previously saved draft is retained for recovery and is not partially reconciled against the invalid snapshot.

### AC-US03-M03 — Published label and order changes preserve masking

**Given** a valid form has one `identityDocument` purpose

**When** an editor changes its label or order and publishes the form

**Then** Summary continues to identify and mask the value through purpose metadata

**And** the unmasked value is absent from visible text and the accessibility tree.

### AC-US03-M04 — Existing persisted state is handled safely

**Given** a browser has a draft or completed receipt written under the previously optional-purpose contract

**When** the updated app restores that state

**Then** it does not expose a raw identity-document value because required purpose metadata is absent from the current form or receipt

**And** it preserves country isolation, completed-quote duplicate protection, and the documented retry or recovery behavior.

The exact migration or fail-closed handling for a legacy terminal receipt is unresolved in Q-US03-M01 and must be decided at the architecture checkpoint before implementation.

## Proposed regression tests

| Test ID | Level | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| T-US03-M01 | Shared contract | Accept one required text identity marker. Reject missing, duplicate, optional, and non-text identity markers. Keep existing valid CO and CL fixtures accepted. |
| T-US03-M02 | Shared contract / Strapi integration | Publish a form with missing, duplicate, or incompatible identity metadata. Verify the projection is unavailable and public output never supplies a usable configuration with the document treated as ordinary unmarked text. |
| T-US03-M03 | Angular unit/component | Verify the approved masking cases for values with separators and Unicode letters or digits, plus visible and accessible output. Verify label and order changes do not affect field identification. |
| T-US03-M04 | Browser regression | In both countries, change and publish the identity field label and order without changing purpose, reload, and verify masking. Publish malformed identity metadata and verify recoverable failure without raw Summary disclosure or partial draft replacement. |
| T-US03-M05 | Storage compatibility | Seed legacy draft and terminal receipt envelopes from the existing released format. Verify the selected migration or fail-closed behavior, terminal route protection, country isolation, and absence of the full document. |

## Questions for architecture review

| ID | Question |
|---|---|
| Q-US03-M01 | For existing version 2 terminal receipts, which have only rendered row strings and no purpose metadata, how should the app preserve the terminal quote reference and duplicate lock while preventing disclosure if a row may contain an unmasked document? Assess an explicit receipt format version, safe legacy display behavior, and the treatment of rows that cannot be identified reliably. |
| Q-US03-M02 | Should a usable form require exactly one required `identityDocument` marker, or should the contract add a dedicated typed sensitive/document field property? Select one consistent approach and document its editorial and compatibility consequences. |
| Q-US03-M03 | What recovery message and action should be offered when identity metadata is malformed while preserving an existing draft or terminal receipt? Reuse current form and terminal error patterns where possible. |

## Approval boundary

This proposal changes ADR-002's optional `identityDocument` marker rule and may change the ADR-005 terminal receipt compatibility contract. Obtain explicit human approval of this specification and any new or amended ADR before implementing code. Preserve the existing approved story specifications, ADRs, and approval records as historical evidence.

| ID | Question |

Document decisions, not just code. The most valuable documentation captures the *why* — the context, constraints, and trade-offs that led to a decision. Code shows *what* was built; documentation explains *why it was built this way* and *what alternatives were considered*. This context is essential for future humans and agents working in the codebase.

## When to Use

- Making a significant architectural decision
- Choosing between competing approaches
- Adding or changing a public API
- Shipping a feature that changes user-facing behavior
- Onboarding new team members (or agents) to the project
- When you find yourself explaining the same thing repeatedly

**When NOT to use:** Don't document obvious code. Don't add comments that restate what the code already says. Don't write docs for throwaway prototypes.

ADRs capture the reasoning behind significant technical decisions. They're the highest-value documentation you can write.

### When to Write an ADR

- Choosing a framework, library, or major dependency

- Any decision that would be expensive to reverse

# ADR-006 — Identity document masking across form revisions and receipt versions

**Status** Proposed, pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-01 form contract and US-03, AC-US03-M01 through AC-US03-M04  
**Basis** [Approved masking correction](../../spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md), [owner approval](../approvals/US-03-identity-masking-spec-approval.md), and [technical assessment](../../requirements/technical-assessment.pdf), page 8

## Context

[ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) permits an optional `identityDocument` purpose. Summary and receipt capture use that purpose to decide which value to mask. Removing the purpose leaves an ordinary text field. Requiring the purpose somewhere in the form still lets an editor move the marker to a second field while the first key retains its saved document value. Both country seeds already use `identity-document` for the document-number field.

[ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps the draft and quote state in the current browser tab. Stored version 1 draft entries carry a key, kind, and value without a record of the previous field purpose. Version 2 receipts from the [ADR-005 terminal amendment](ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md) contain rendered rows with opaque IDs and no masking provenance. Their reference and country can be validated independently of the review.

## Proposed decision

### Bind identity purpose to the existing stable key

Amend ADR-002 to require exactly one required text field with the paired ID `identity-document` and purpose `identityDocument` in each country. The ID is reserved for that purpose and the purpose is valid only on that ID. The shared decoder enforces both directions for Strapi's public projection and Angular's response boundary. Keep form schema version 1, the existing endpoint and public permissions, and the existing `Cache-Control: no-store` behavior. The seeded forms already satisfy the requirement.

Editors retain control of labels, order, help, and supported validation settings. Field keys keep their semantic meaning across revisions. For a custom published form using a different document ID, update the existing identity field to the reserved key in Strapi. Remove any redundant document capture field before republishing. A custom form needing that correction remains unavailable until corrected. The shared contract identifies declared field semantics. Arbitrary sensitive content placed by an editor or entered by a user into a different field is outside its classification guarantee.

Reject an invalid snapshot atomically, including a missing, swapped, duplicate, optional, or wrong-kind identity field. Strapi reuses its `503 FORM_UNAVAILABLE` response for invalid published content. Angular reuses the configuration unavailable state and Retry. It must leave the draft untouched while the snapshot is invalid and must not show Summary or enable Pay against that invalid response. Reuse same-country form loading, explicit refresh, and response generation checks. An already loaded valid snapshot may finish under the existing flow because the identity binding is invariant in every accepted snapshot. During any refresh, ready state and a current validated draft remain prerequisites. Completed receipts remain independent of live configuration.

### Reconcile legacy drafts before they can feed Summary

Keep the country-scoped draft key and introduce a version 2 envelope for drafts normalized under this contract. On the first successful load of a valid form, reconcile a version 1 draft into the new format. Preserve a compatible value at the reserved identity key for the existing masked projection. Clear legacy text and date values at other keys. An unmarked document may have been entered at an arbitrary text key and a date-shaped string may have survived the existing text-to-date reconciliation. The old format cannot prove those values safe to display. Retain compatible number, select, and checkbox entries using normal reconciliation. Cleared fields are unset so required fields must be re-entered and an existing value is never copied to a new semantic role. Preserve country isolation and the ordinary in-memory fallback if writing the normalized draft fails. The same safe migration repeats after reload when storage still holds version 1.

Use the existing shared masking rule in the one review projector consumed by Summary and approval capture. The projector receives only the current decoded form and its reconciled draft. Classify the reserved row at that boundary and mask its value before creating any visible or accessible row. Keep the raw value in the editable draft. Plan, terms, consent and payment behavior from ADR-005 continue to apply.

### Treat a receipt's terminal reference independently of its review

Use the existing per-country receipt key with envelope version 3 for new approvals. Preserve the ordered projection, plan name and typed price. Use a discriminated row within the ordered review for the reserved identity ID, carrying the already masked display value, and ordinary rows for all other IDs. Require exactly one masked identity row. Validate the reserved ID association, unique IDs, bounded strings and country money using existing limits. Reject an identity display value with no mask glyph before any exposed alphanumeric character or with more than four exposed alphanumeric characters. Continue to apply the approved short-value and separator rules at capture. The row variant and shape checks establish an application format boundary. Session storage has no authenticity guarantee against code running in the same origin.

| Stored envelope | Restore decision |
| --- | --- |
| Version 1 with valid country, reference, and original size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Reuse the existing detail-unavailable state. |
| Version 2 with valid country, reference, and envelope size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Discard the entire review, including all labels and plan metadata. No row ID, label, value, or live form can establish its historical masking provenance. |
| Version 3 with valid country, reference, and envelope size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Render the immutable review only after full validation. If the review fails validation, use the reference-only state. |
| Unknown version, invalid header, wrong country, excessive size, or unparseable data | Render no stored content and do not infer an approval from untrusted bytes. A terminal receipt already held in memory retains its lock. |

Retain the existing pre-parse size limit for versions 2 and 3, including worst-case escaped values, and validate the quote reference using the current strict format. Never migrate old receipt rows through a rewrite, re-mask them heuristically, or reconstruct them from a draft or live CMS. Restore takes place before editable route state or content requests. The restored reference alone blocks all same-country wizard edits and Pay, including direct navigation, Back, Forward, and reload. Switching to the other country remains independent. Failed writes retain the masked version 3 projection and lock in memory with the existing reload limitation. Restart uses the current cleanup sequence. Verify draft and plan removal first, delete the single receipt key as the durable commit point, then release the in-memory lock last. Any failed cleanup preserves the terminal guard and supports retry. No new stores, libraries, or network access are required.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Require a unique purpose on any ID | The marker can move to another field while leaving the old document input and its value on an ordinary field. A reserved pair avoids that transition and matches both seeds. |
| Infer identity from labels, pattern, or value | Localization and valid edits make these signals unreliable. |
| Keep other legacy review rows or re-mask selected rows | Legacy rows carry no reliable identity provenance. Reference-only restoration gives up historical detail and keeps the approval and restart behavior. |
| Purge the full legacy draft or carry every legacy field forward | Full purge loses safe selections and compatible canonical identity data. Full carry-forward can display a value from a former unmarked document field. The migration clears only ambiguous legacy string categories outside the canonical field. |
| Store raw receipt values for replay or add a second key | Raw storage increases exposure. A second key creates reset and recovery coordination without improving the masking guarantee. |

## Verification

# ADR-006 — Identity document masking across form revisions and receipt versions

**Status** Proposed, pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-01 form contract and US-03, AC-US03-M01 through AC-US03-M04  
**Basis** [Approved masking correction](../../spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md), [owner approval](../approvals/US-03-identity-masking-spec-approval.md), and [technical assessment](../../requirements/technical-assessment.pdf), page 8

## Context

[ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) permits an optional `identityDocument` purpose. Summary and receipt capture use that purpose to decide which value to mask. Removing the purpose leaves an ordinary text field. Requiring the purpose somewhere in the form still lets an editor move the marker to a second field while the first key retains its saved document value. Both country seeds already use `identity-document` for the document-number field.

[ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps the draft and quote state in the current browser tab. Stored version 1 draft entries carry a key, kind, and value without a record of the previous field purpose. Version 2 receipts from the [ADR-005 terminal amendment](ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md) contain rendered rows with opaque IDs and no masking provenance. Their reference and country can be validated independently of the review.

## Proposed decision

### Bind identity purpose to the existing stable key

Amend ADR-002 to require exactly one required text field with the paired ID `identity-document` and purpose `identityDocument` in each country. The ID is reserved for that purpose and the purpose is valid only on that ID. The shared decoder enforces both directions for Strapi's public projection and Angular's response boundary. Keep form schema version 1, the existing endpoint and public permissions, and the existing `Cache-Control: no-store` behavior. The seeded forms already satisfy the requirement.

Editors retain control of labels, order, help, and supported validation settings. Field keys keep their semantic meaning across revisions. For a custom published form using a different document ID, update the existing identity field to the reserved key in Strapi. Remove any redundant document capture field before republishing. A custom form needing that correction remains unavailable until corrected. The shared contract identifies declared field semantics. Arbitrary sensitive content placed by an editor or entered by a user into a different field is outside its classification guarantee.

Reject an invalid snapshot atomically, including a missing, swapped, duplicate, optional, or wrong-kind identity field. Strapi reuses its `503 FORM_UNAVAILABLE` response for invalid published content. Angular reuses the configuration unavailable state and Retry. It must leave the draft untouched while the snapshot is invalid and must not show Summary or enable Pay against that invalid response. Reuse same-country form loading, explicit refresh, and response generation checks. An already loaded valid snapshot may finish under the existing flow because the identity binding is invariant in every accepted snapshot. During any refresh, ready state and a current validated draft remain prerequisites. Completed receipts remain independent of live configuration.

### Reconcile legacy drafts before they can feed Summary

Keep the country-scoped draft key and introduce a version 2 envelope for drafts normalized under this contract. On the first successful load of a valid form, reconcile a version 1 draft into the new format. Preserve a compatible value at the reserved identity key for the existing masked projection. Clear legacy text and date values at other keys. An unmarked document may have been entered at an arbitrary text key and a date-shaped string may have survived the existing text-to-date reconciliation. The old format cannot prove those values safe to display. Retain compatible number, select, and checkbox entries using normal reconciliation. Cleared fields are unset so required fields must be re-entered and an existing value is never copied to a new semantic role. Preserve country isolation and the ordinary in-memory fallback if writing the normalized draft fails. The same safe migration repeats after reload when storage still holds version 1.

Use the existing shared masking rule in the one review projector consumed by Summary and approval capture. The projector receives only the current decoded form and its reconciled draft. Classify the reserved row at that boundary and mask its value before creating any visible or accessible row. Keep the raw value in the editable draft. Plan, terms, consent and payment behavior from ADR-005 continue to apply.

### Treat a receipt's terminal reference independently of its review

Use the existing per-country receipt key with envelope version 3 for new approvals. Preserve the ordered projection, plan name and typed price. Use a discriminated row within the ordered review for the reserved identity ID, carrying the already masked display value, and ordinary rows for all other IDs. Require exactly one masked identity row. Validate the reserved ID association, unique IDs, bounded strings and country money using existing limits. Reject an identity display value with no mask glyph before any exposed alphanumeric character or with more than four exposed alphanumeric characters. Continue to apply the approved short-value and separator rules at capture. The row variant and shape checks establish an application format boundary. Session storage has no authenticity guarantee against code running in the same origin.

| Stored envelope | Restore decision |
| --- | --- |
| Version 1 with valid country, reference, and original size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Reuse the existing detail-unavailable state. |
| Version 2 with valid country, reference, and envelope size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Discard the entire review, including all labels and plan metadata. No row ID, label, value, or live form can establish its historical masking provenance. |
| Version 3 with valid country, reference, and envelope size bound | Restore reference and terminal lock. Render the immutable review only after full validation. If the review fails validation, use the reference-only state. |
| Unknown version, invalid header, wrong country, excessive size, or unparseable data | Render no stored content and do not infer an approval from untrusted bytes. A terminal receipt already held in memory retains its lock. |

Retain the existing pre-parse size limit for versions 2 and 3, including worst-case escaped values, and validate the quote reference using the current strict format. Never migrate old receipt rows through a rewrite, re-mask them heuristically, or reconstruct them from a draft or live CMS. Restore takes place before editable route state or content requests. The restored reference alone blocks all same-country wizard edits and Pay, including direct navigation, Back, Forward, and reload. Switching to the other country remains independent. Failed writes retain the masked version 3 projection and lock in memory with the existing reload limitation. Restart uses the current cleanup sequence. Verify draft and plan removal first, delete the single receipt key as the durable commit point, then release the in-memory lock last. Any failed cleanup preserves the terminal guard and supports retry. No new stores, libraries, or network access are required.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Require a unique purpose on any ID | The marker can move to another field while leaving the old document input and its value on an ordinary field. A reserved pair avoids that transition and matches both seeds. |
| Infer identity from labels, pattern, or value | Localization and valid edits make these signals unreliable. |
| Keep other legacy review rows or re-mask selected rows | Legacy rows carry no reliable identity provenance. Reference-only restoration gives up historical detail and keeps the approval and restart behavior. |
| Purge the full legacy draft or carry every legacy field forward | Full purge loses safe selections and compatible canonical identity data. Full carry-forward can display a value from a former unmarked document field. The migration clears only ambiguous legacy string categories outside the canonical field. |
| Store raw receipt values for replay or add a second key | Raw storage increases exposure. A second key creates reset and recovery coordination without improving the masking guarantee. |

# Git Workflow and Versioning

## Overview

Git is your safety net. Treat commits as save points, branches as sandboxes, and history as documentation. With AI agents generating code at high speed, disciplined version control is the mechanism that keeps changes manageable, reviewable, and reversible.

## When to Use

Always. Every code change flows through git.

## Core Principles

### Trunk-Based Development (Recommended)

Keep `main` always deployable. Work in short-lived feature branches that merge back within 1-3 days. Long-lived development branches are hidden costs — they diverge, create merge conflicts, and delay integration. DORA research consistently shows trunk-based development correlates with high-performing engineering teams.

# Git Workflow and Versioning

## Overview

Git is your safety net. Treat commits as save points, branches as sandboxes, and history as documentation. With AI agents generating code at high speed, disciplined version control is the mechanism that keeps changes manageable, reviewable, and reversible.

## When to Use

Always. Every code change flows through git.

## Core Principles

### Trunk-Based Development (Recommended)

Keep `main` always deployable. Work in short-lived feature branches that merge back within 1-3 days. Long-lived development branches are hidden costs — they diverge, create merge conflicts, and delay integration. DORA research consistently shows trunk-based development correlates with high-performing engineering teams.

### Final compliance follow-up · US-03 masking specification approval

- The owner explicitly approved the [masking correction specification](spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md) and requested an architecture assessment through its approval checkpoint. The orchestrator recorded the [approval and draft hash](docs/approvals/US-03-identity-masking-spec-approval.md), preserving the earlier US-03 decisions.
- The orchestrator delegated one proposed ADR to `/root/mask_arch` (Architect, `gpt-6.2-sol` / `high` as configured). The prompt scoped the assessment to CMS masking invariants, receipt compatibility, preservation of the quote reference and terminal lock, and regression traceability. It directed the Architect to reuse the approved architecture and leave design and implementation for later checkpoints.

- The Architect used `spec-driven-development`, `angular-developer`, and cached `modern-web-guidance` privacy guidance. The resulting [ADR-006 proposal](docs/adr/ADR-006-identity-document-masking.md) pairs the existing identity key with its purpose, defines conservative legacy draft reconciliation, and restores legacy receipts by reference while retaining their terminal lock. It proposes a versioned masked review for new receipts using the existing storage key and reset sequence. Repository evidence identifies the collaboration path. A native session ID and unedited export were not verified.
- The orchestrator checked the approved specification hash, local ADR links, acceptance and regression test identifiers, and read-only Git status. Architecture approval is pending. Design and implementation have not begun.

### Final compliance follow-up · US-03 masking architecture approval

- The owner explicitly approved [ADR-006](docs/adr/ADR-006-identity-document-masking.md). The orchestrator recorded the [decision and reviewed proposal hash](docs/approvals/US-03-identity-masking-architecture-approval.md), verified that the ADR changed only in approval metadata, and closed the approval checkpoint. Design and implementation have not begun.

## Skill selection and controls

The project-specific `story-to-spec` skill defines the insurance assessment source and specification format. Other installed skills are third-party workflow or technical guidance. Select skills by stage and task as listed in `AGENTS.md`. Conditional skills are loaded only when the work warrants them. Project instructions and assessment requirements take precedence over conflicting skill guidance. Skills do not bypass security restrictions or human approval checkpoints. Record skills actually used in execution evidence and keep this proposed flow distinct from completed work.

## Git conventions and authorization

Use English Conventional Commit messages in `<type>(<optional-scope>): <description>` format, with focused atomic changes. Suggest a commit message when work is ready. Staging, committing, pushing, merging, branch creation or deletion, history rewriting, and destructive Git actions each require explicit human authorization for that operation. Approval of a specification or code does not grant Git authorization. Read-only Git inspection is allowed. Never place credentials, secrets, personal data, or sensitive information in commits or logs.

## Model allocation and usage

Keep the configured model and effort assignments from `docs/agent-model-policy.md`. Choose the least number of agents and skills needed for a task. Avoid loading all skills or invoking agents without a concrete independent responsibility. The project targets a ChatGPT Plus subscription, so use focused prompts, narrow source reads, sequential checkpoints, and only the context needed for each stage. Do not claim a subscription allowance, cost, or usage outcome that has not been verified.

## Traceability and verification levels

Maintain `User Story → spec/US-XX.md → applicable approved ADRs → approved design (when requested) → implementation → stable test case IDs → reports/qa/US-XX-qa-report.md → reviews/US-XX-review.md → finding resolution evidence → human approval`. Reference repository paths and actual evidence. Reuse approved ADRs when they cover the story. Story reports cover the current story only. Complete quote-flow and cross-country verification are project-level checks before final delivery, not prerequisites for each story when later stories are pending.

## Retrospective

### How would this flow change for a five-developer team?
Assign a human owner to each story and a maintainer to the shared form, plan, and terms contracts. Run independent work in parallel once its spec and ADRs are approved. For example, QA can prepare country fixtures while implementation proceeds, while changes to shared contracts need coordinated review before dependent work lands. Use a shared review queue and automated unit, CMS integration, and two-country browser checks so every reviewer sees the same evidence before handoff.

### What did not work as expected, and what changed?
US-01 independent QA hit a model usage limit before the report was ready. The owner chose to retry the original QA agent using existing evidence, and that agent resumed without a model substitution. In US-03, the Angular development server returned its SPA fallback for API requests expected to return 404. QA moved the full browser suite to the static Compose deployment, where the route assertions passed. These incidents showed where to retain verified partial results and where to run checks against the delivery environment.

### Where did we deliberately avoid using AI, and why?
The owner made the specification, architecture, design, and final acceptance decisions. For example, the owner requested removal of the wizard header country controls and accepted the terminal quote revision after manual verification. The owner also authorized Git operations separately. These decisions established business intent, accepted implementation trade-offs, and controlled repository changes. Agents prepared and verified the supporting artifacts.

Both countries also exercised an injected receipt-key deletion failure: the error was announced, focus stayed on the restart control, and reload restored the original terminal receipt. Keyboard retry cleared the active country's prior entered data, selected plan and receipt, opened same-country Details with focus on its heading, and prevented the old Summary history entry from restoring the receipt. A subsequent approval created a different reference. A legacy version 1 reference-only Colombia receipt remained terminal and reset successfully. The existing rejection, edit, plan retention and retry-to-approval cases passed for both countries in the same full-suite run.

The first focused terminal run passed the legacy case but four country cases failed because the test compared multiline `innerText()` with Playwright's normalized `toHaveText()` representation. After correcting that comparison, an expanded run found two more test-only reset expectation failures: Angular's configured select placeholder has DOM value `0: null`, so the tests were updated to assert the selected placeholder label instead. No application defect was indicated by either test-authoring mismatch. The corrected focused run passed 5/5; the final full browser suite passed 27/27. The final tests include keyboard reset and focus checks. This run did not modify CMS content.

## QA recommendation

The US-03 base scope, copy revision and terminal quote revision passed dedicated browser, CMS integration, unit and full cross-story browser coverage. US03-QA-01 is resolved with evidence. No blocking implementation defect was reproduced. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks remain unverified.

## Identity masking correction re-verification, 2026-11-22

**Status:** QA pass for the approved US-03 identity masking correction. No confirmed implementation defect remains in the verified scope. Independent Reviewer re-review and final human approval remain pending.

### Story and traceability

- **User story:** US-03 — Summary and payment, with the shared US-01 dynamic form contract.
- **Approved correction specification:** [spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md](../../spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md).
- **Approved architecture:** [ADR-006](../../docs/adr/ADR-006-identity-document-masking.md), with existing ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-005, and the terminal quote amendment.
- **QA agent:** /root/mask_qa, configured and used as gpt-6-luna / xhigh.
- **Skills:** test-driven-development and Angular testing guidance. I inspected the browser-testing-with-devtools guidance. The Chrome DevTools MCP server was not available, so browser verification used the repository's Playwright setup and installed Google Chrome.
- **Environment:** Node 24.15.0, pnpm 11.29.0, Playwright 1.65.1, Google Chrome, and an isolated production Compose stack at 127.0.0.1:18085 with a fresh Strapi volume at 127.0.0.1:18385. The default local Compose stack and content were not used or changed.

### Acceptance results

| Acceptance criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-US03-M01 — One required identity field uses the reserved key and purpose | Pass | pnpm test passed 17 shared tests. The decoder tests cover both country fixtures and reject a missing or moved marker, duplicate identity meaning, optional identity field, and incompatible field kind. |
| AC-US03-M02 — Invalid identity metadata fails closed | Pass | T-US03-M02/M05 passed in both countries. An invalid initial response showed the existing form unavailable/Retry state, withheld the saved raw strings, and left the legacy draft byte-for-byte unchanged. Retry with a valid response restored the form. Live Strapi publication checks returned 503 FORM_UNAVAILABLE for invalid identity metadata in both countries and 200 after repair. |
| AC-US03-M03 — Valid labels and order changes preserve masking | Pass | T-US03-M03/M04 passed in both countries. The browser received the actual published country response with the identity label changed and order moved to the first field. Summary and receipt rendered the new label and masked value. A live Strapi integration check independently published and read valid label/order changes for CO and CL with the reserved identity purpose intact. |
| AC-US03-M04 — Legacy state does not disclose unverified values | Pass | T-US03-M04/M05 passed in both countries. Legacy v1 and v2 receipts retained their quote reference and terminal route while their detail rows were withheld. Raw legacy values were absent from visible and accessible body text. Reset cleared the receipt and opened blank Details. Legacy v1 draft recovery preserved the reserved identity value, cleared ambiguous text/date values under other IDs, and migrated to draft version 2 after a valid form response. |

### Tests executed

| Command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| CI=1 pnpm test | Passed. 17 shared contract tests and 30 Angular tests across three files. |
| pnpm test:content | Passed. 2 Strapi integration tests. The public content lifecycle test exercised valid identity label/order publication, invalid marker publication and recovery in both countries. |
| QUOTE_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome QUOTE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18085 QUOTE_CMS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18385 pnpm exec playwright test e2e/us03-masking-qa.spec.ts --workers=1 | Passed 8/8 focused masking cases across Colombia and Chile. |
| QUOTE_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome QUOTE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18085 QUOTE_CMS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18385 pnpm exec playwright test --workers=1 | Passed 35/35 browser tests across US-01, US-02, US-03, and the masking correction on the isolated stack. |
| pnpm exec prettier --check e2e/us03-masking-qa.spec.ts backend/test/public-content.test.mjs | Passed. |
| git diff --check | Passed. |

### Run history and limits

The first Chrome launch under the default sandbox terminated before any browser assertion. Re-running with the permitted loopback/browser access completed. The first focused test draft also had QA fixture mistakes: it used an incorrect holder field ID and tried to inspect Summary before selecting a plan. After correcting the test setup, all eight focused cases passed. These were test harness issues, not reproduced product defects.

The browser modified the published form response for valid label/order cases through Playwright's response handler. The separate disposable Strapi integration test independently verified that valid changes publish and project correctly and that invalid identity metadata fails closed. No edits were made to the default Strapi volume.

The regression suite verifies text present in the DOM and an accessibility snapshot. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks were not performed. Corrupted and invalid version 3 receipt shapes are also covered by frontend/src/app/quote/quote-receipt.spec.ts in the 30 passing Angular tests. No real identity data was used.

### Findings and recommendation

- **Confirmed product defects:** none.
- **QA finding:** none opened.
- **Recommendation:** QA pass for AC-US03-M01 through AC-US03-M04. Independent Reviewer re-review and final human approval remain necessary before QA handoff.

- The terms endpoint selects published country documents only, limits the result to two to detect duplicates, projects only country and body, computes the revision from the displayed text and returns `no-store`. QA verified the Public role grants and request boundary.
- Terms are rendered through Angular interpolation. The decoder validates country, revision format, nonblank content and size before the response enters state.
- The payment command reserves the attempt synchronously by moving to `checking` before the terms refresh. Repeated activation is guarded by `canPay`, and the captured country, generation and quote snapshot are checked before processing and settlement. Navigation cancels the request/timer and invalidates late callbacks.
- The selected document is masked in the read-only review projection. The consent snapshot uses a per-country draft revision, field identifiers and kinds, selected plan ID and final price. The draft revision advances only when underlying normalized field values or kinds change, so edits to a hidden identity prefix invalidate consent even when the visible mask is unchanged.
- Receipts contain only a version, country and opaque random quote reference in bounded tab storage. Restore validates version, country and reference. The terminal receipt route bypasses editable Summary and prevents duplicate payment. Interrupted payment state and consent remain memory-only.
- Native radio controls, an associated consent label, visible feedback and a status region follow the approved design. QA exercised keyboard operation and mobile reflow.

## Recommendation

**Approved.** The reviewed changes implement the approved US-03 specification, ADR-005 and design, and QA evidence covers both countries and the complete successful and rejected payment retry flows. Native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast verification remain unverified for the project-level delivery record.

## Targeted copy re-review, 2026-11-22

The project owner requested a focused copy change after the initial review. I re-reviewed the current Summary and Details copy, the updated demo outcome label and Pay action, the seed help-text change, the copy assertions in `e2e/us03-qa.spec.ts`, and the scoped live content correction recorded in `FLOW.md` and the QA report.

- **Result group:** The fieldset legend is `Resultado de prueba` at `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-summary.html:92-94`. Together with the Approved and Rejected native choices, it identifies the control as a deterministic test outcome.
- **Payment action:** The single payment and retry button is labeled `Pagar` at `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-summary.html:129-137`.
- **Removed copy:** The fictitious-data introduction and the identity field's `Usa un número ficticio.` help text are absent from the active Details presentation. The seed now initializes that help text empty at `backend/src/seed-forms.ts:92-102`. QA's country flows assert both strings are absent.
- **Summary and receipt copy:** QA asserts the previous `Resultado del pago (solo demostración)` legend, `No se realizará un cobro real.` sentence and `Simular pago` button are absent, and checks the receipt for the requested country-neutral copy. The approved terms and payment error/rejection feedback remain available. Loading, checking and processing announcements remain in the status region required for accessible operation.
- **Existing CMS content:** The workflow records that the default local SQLite volume held the old identity help text in four matching draft and published components. The orchestrator backed up that database and cleared only those matching help-text values in one transaction. Both published country form reads then reported empty document help, and the QA flows on the rebuilt default Compose stack verified that the hint no longer appeared. The developer also updated the fresh-install seed. The QA report records the initial Colombia brand-fixture mismatch and the corrected helper now selects the first configured brand option, avoiding a hard-coded content label.
- **Verification:** The QA report records a focused rerun of both country flows (2/2) and the complete dedicated US-03 suite (5/5) against the rebuilt default Compose app. The copy checks, rejection/retry with owner and plan retained, approval, receipt reload and existing CMS terms routes passed.

No new finding. The copy changes and scoped content update are consistent with the owner's request and preserve the approved payment behavior and accessibility status announcements. The original approval recommendation stands.

## Terminal quote revision re-review, 2026-11-22

Reviewed the approved [terminal quote specification](../spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md), [ADR-005 amendment](../docs/adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md), and [design revision](../docs/design/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md) against the implementation, focused tests, and updated QA report.

- **Route protection and country scope:** The route parameter handler checks the canonical country receipt synchronously before loading form or plan content. A receipt redirects same-country Details and Plans history/direct entries to Summary, where only the confirmation component renders. Receipt state remains keyed per country. QA's CO and CL browser cases verified direct navigation, Back/Forward, reload, no transient editable controls, no live content reads, and continued independence of the other country.
- **Frozen receipt:** The v2 record stores only the quote reference, country, ordered display rows, plan name and validated final price. The identity value is masked before capture. The decoder enforces the 200,000-character envelope cap, row and string bounds, unique safe IDs, country-specific currency, version and receipt format. Rendering uses decoded strings as text. A v2 validation failure does not fall back to the reference-only format.
- **Legacy receipt:** Version 1 references retain terminal routing and the restart action without attempting to reconstruct historical details from mutable form or plan state. Reset removes the shared country receipt key for either version.
- **Restart durability and races:** Restart retains the receipt in memory, invalidates form, plan, terms and payment work, verifies draft and plan key removal, then removes the terminal key as its commit point. Failure before that point leaves the terminal view retryable. After commit it clears country memory state and releases the receipt guard before same-country Details navigation. The route checks also guard advancement and plan continuation against a receipt. QA exercised failure at receipt deletion with reload and retry in both countries, per-key failures in Angular tests, blank defaults after reset, preserved other-country keys, old history protection, a new reference, and focus on Details.
- **Payment retry and tests:** Rejection remains on editable Summary and preserves the prior same-country edit, plan and fresh-terms retry path. QA reports the 27/27 full Chrome suite against the isolated production Compose stack, including the prior rejection/retry cases and five terminal revision browser cases. Focused storage tests cover receipt versions, malformed records and reset failure stages.

No new finding. The terminal quote revision follows its approved spec, ADR amendment and design. The original approval recommendation remains in effect. QA still records native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks as unverified.

## Identity masking correction re-review, 2026-11-22

Reviewed the approved [identity masking correction specification](../spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md) and [ADR-006](../docs/adr/ADR-006-identity-document-masking.md) against the implementation and the appended QA evidence in [US-03 QA](../reports/qa/US-03-qa-report.md). The worktree contained implementation and documentation changes during this review, so I inspected the current diff and code but did not run mutating probes or tests from the shared checkout.

- **Form and CMS boundary:** `shared/src/index.ts` binds the unique `identityDocument` purpose to the required text field with ID `identity-document`, rejects missing or moved purpose metadata, and requires the marker in every decoded form. The same decoder validates both the Strapi projection and browser response. The live CMS tests and fresh-stack reads reported by QA verify valid label/order edits and 503 rejection/recovery for both CO and CL.
- **Summary and receipt projection:** `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-review.ts` identifies the reserved key, applies the established masking rule before building presentation rows, and tags that row for receipt validation. `quote-payment.ts` stores newly completed reviews as version 3. The version 3 decoder in `quote-receipt.ts` requires one identity row with the reserved key and accepted mask shape, validates ordinary rows and price, and degrades a malformed review to reference-only terminal state. The rendered review uses the same plain text row projection for visible and accessible content.
- **Legacy drafts:** `quote-state.ts` preserves the canonical identity value for the masked projection and clears ambiguous version 1 text/date values at other keys before reconciliation. Invalid form responses do not call reconciliation or save, so the previous draft remains intact for Retry. Both-country browser coverage verified withheld values on the error screen, byte-for-byte retention, migration after valid recovery, and blank ambiguous values.
- **Legacy and terminal behavior:** Receipt versions 1 and 2 restore only the validated quote reference. Version 2 row labels, values and plan details are discarded. The route guard consumes the reference as terminal state, preserving duplicate-payment prevention and the established restart flow. QA verified reload, attempted Plans navigation, absence of editable controls, reference retention and reset for both countries.
- **Regression coverage and evidence:** QA reports 17 shared and 30 Angular tests passing, two CMS integration tests passing, eight focused masking browser cases passing, and the full 35-test Playwright suite passing on an isolated production-style Compose stack. I inspected the associated test changes and the recorded results. I did not independently execute them because the shared worktree was dirty and the review role was limited to review artifacts. Native screen-reader and OS high-contrast checks remain outside this correction's verification.
- **Scope boundary:** The approved ADR guarantees classification for the reserved identity field. Sensitive content placed in a different CMS field remains outside that field-purpose contract, as ADR-006 states. Editors must preserve the semantic identity of field keys and use the reserved ID/purpose for policyholder documents.

**Finding history:** No new findings. Existing US-03 findings and their resolutions above are preserved.

**Recommendation:** **Approved.** The implementation follows the approved correction and ADR, closes the identified unmasked identity path under supported form changes, withholds unverified legacy review values, and preserves reference-only terminal locking and reset behavior. Final human approval remains pending.

A receipt redirects same-country Details and Plans history/direct entries to Summary, where only the confirmation component renders. Receipt state remains keyed per country. QA's CO and CL browser cases verified direct navigation, Back/Forward, reload, no transient editable controls, no live content reads, and continued independence of the other country.
- **Frozen receipt:** The v2 record stores only the quote reference, country, ordered display rows, plan name and validated final price. The identity value is masked before capture. The decoder enforces the 200,000-character envelope cap, row and string bounds, unique safe IDs, country-specific currency, version and receipt format. Rendering uses decoded strings as text. A v2 validation failure does not fall back to the reference-only format.
- **Legacy receipt:** Version 1 references retain terminal routing and the restart action without attempting to reconstruct historical details from mutable form or plan state. Reset removes the shared country receipt key for either version.
- **Restart durability and races:** Restart retains the receipt in memory, invalidates form, plan, terms and payment work, verifies draft and plan key removal, then removes the terminal key as its commit point. Failure before that point leaves the terminal view retryable. After commit it clears country memory state and releases the receipt guard before same-country Details navigation. The route checks also guard advancement and plan continuation against a receipt. QA exercised failure at receipt deletion with reload and retry in both countries, per-key failures in Angular tests, blank defaults after reset, preserved other-country keys, old history protection, a new reference, and focus on Details.
- **Payment retry and tests:** Rejection remains on editable Summary and preserves the prior same-country edit, plan and fresh-terms retry path. QA reports the 27/27 full Chrome suite against the isolated production Compose stack, including the prior rejection/retry cases and five terminal revision browser cases. Focused storage tests cover receipt versions, malformed records and reset failure stages.

No new finding. The terminal quote revision follows its approved spec, ADR amendment and design. The original approval recommendation remains in effect. QA still records native screen-reader and operating-system high-contrast checks as unverified.

## Identity masking correction re-review, 2026-11-22

Reviewed the approved [identity masking correction specification](../spec/US-03-identity-masking-correction.md) and [ADR-006](../docs/adr/ADR-006-identity-document-masking.md) against the implementation and the appended QA evidence in [US-03 QA](../reports/qa/US-03-qa-report.md). The worktree contained implementation and documentation changes during this review, so I inspected the current diff and code but did not run mutating probes or tests from the shared checkout.

- **Form and CMS boundary:** `shared/src/index.ts` binds the unique `identityDocument` purpose to the required text field with ID `identity-document`, rejects missing or moved purpose metadata, and requires the marker in every decoded form. The same decoder validates both the Strapi projection and browser response. The live CMS tests and fresh-stack reads reported by QA verify valid label/order edits and 503 rejection/recovery for both CO and CL.
- **Summary and receipt projection:** `frontend/src/app/quote/quote-review.ts` identifies the reserved key, applies the established masking rule before building presentation rows, and tags that row for receipt validation. `quote-payment.ts` stores newly completed reviews as version 3. The version 3 decoder in `quote-receipt.ts` requires one identity row with the reserved key and accepted mask shape, validates ordinary rows and price, and degrades a malformed review to reference-only terminal state. The rendered review uses the same plain text row projection for visible and accessible content.
- **Legacy drafts:** `quote-state.ts` preserves the canonical identity value for the masked projection and clears ambiguous version 1 text/date values at other keys before reconciliation. Invalid form responses do not call reconciliation or save, so the previous draft remains intact for Retry. Both-country browser coverage verified withheld values on the error screen, byte-for-byte retention, migration after valid recovery, and blank ambiguous values.
- **Legacy and terminal behavior:** Receipt versions 1 and 2 restore only the validated quote reference. Version 2 row labels, values and plan details are discarded. The route guard consumes the reference as terminal state, preserving duplicate-payment prevention and the established restart flow. QA verified reload, attempted Plans navigation, absence of editable controls, reference retention and reset for both countries.
- **Regression coverage and evidence:** QA reports 17 shared and 30 Angular tests passing, two CMS integration tests passing, eight focused masking browser cases passing, and the full 35-test Playwright suite passing on an isolated production-style Compose stack. I inspected the associated test changes and the recorded results. I did not independently execute them because the shared worktree was dirty and the review role was limited to review artifacts. Native screen-reader and OS high-contrast checks remain outside this correction's verification.
- **Scope boundary:** The approved ADR guarantees classification for the reserved identity field. Sensitive content placed in a different CMS field remains outside that field-purpose contract, as ADR-006 states. Editors must preserve the semantic identity of field keys and use the reserved ID/purpose for policyholder documents.

**Finding history:** No new findings. Existing US-03 findings and their resolutions above are preserved.

**Recommendation:** **Approved.** The implementation follows the approved correction and ADR, closes the identified unmasked identity path under supported form changes, withholds unverified legacy review values, and preserves reference-only terminal locking and reset behavior. Final human approval remains pending.

FLOW.md:374:## Retrospective

Use English Conventional Commit messages in `<type>(<optional-scope>): <description>` format, with focused atomic changes. Suggest a commit message when work is ready. Staging, committing, pushing, merging, branch creation or deletion, history rewriting, and destructive Git actions each require explicit human authorization for that operation. Approval of a specification or code does not grant Git authorization. Read-only Git inspection is allowed. Never place credentials, secrets, personal data, or sensitive information in commits or logs.

## Model allocation and usage

Keep the configured model and effort assignments from `docs/agent-model-policy.md`. Choose the least number of agents and skills needed for a task. Avoid loading all skills or invoking agents without a concrete independent responsibility. The project targets a ChatGPT Plus subscription, so use focused prompts, narrow source reads, sequential checkpoints, and only the context needed for each stage. Do not claim a subscription allowance, cost, or usage outcome that has not been verified.

## Traceability and verification levels

Maintain `User Story → spec/US-XX.md → applicable approved ADRs → approved design (when requested) → implementation → stable test case IDs → reports/qa/US-XX-qa-report.md → reviews/US-XX-review.md → finding resolution evidence → human approval`. Reference repository paths and actual evidence. Reuse approved ADRs when they cover the story. Story reports cover the current story only. Complete quote-flow and cross-country verification are project-level checks before final delivery, not prerequisites for each story when later stories are pending.

## Retrospective

### How would this flow change for a five-developer team?
Assign a human owner to each story and a maintainer to the shared form, plan, and terms contracts. Run independent work in parallel once its spec and ADRs are approved. For example, QA can prepare country fixtures while implementation proceeds, while changes to shared contracts need coordinated review before dependent work lands. Use a shared review queue and automated unit, CMS integration, and two-country browser checks so every reviewer sees the same evidence before handoff.

### What did not work as expected, and what changed?
US-01 independent QA hit a model usage limit before the report was ready. The owner chose to retry the original QA agent using existing evidence, and that agent resumed without a model substitution. In US-03, the Angular development server returned its SPA fallback for API requests expected to return 404. QA moved the full browser suite to the static Compose deployment, where the route assertions passed. These incidents showed where to retain verified partial results and where to run checks against the delivery environment.

### Where did we deliberately avoid using AI, and why?
The owner made the specification, architecture, design, and final acceptance decisions. For example, the owner requested removal of the wizard header country controls and accepted the terminal quote revision after manual verification. The owner also authorized Git operations separately. These decisions established business intent, accepted implementation trade-offs, and controlled repository changes. Agents prepared and verified the supporting artifacts.

FLOW.md:374:## Retrospective

Use English Conventional Commit messages in `<type>(<optional-scope>): <description>` format, with focused atomic changes. Suggest a commit message when work is ready. Staging, committing, pushing, merging, branch creation or deletion, history rewriting, and destructive Git actions each require explicit human authorization for that operation. Approval of a specification or code does not grant Git authorization. Read-only Git inspection is allowed. Never place credentials, secrets, personal data, or sensitive information in commits or logs.

## Model allocation and usage

Keep the configured model and effort assignments from `docs/agent-model-policy.md`. Choose the least number of agents and skills needed for a task. Avoid loading all skills or invoking agents without a concrete independent responsibility. The project targets a ChatGPT Plus subscription, so use focused prompts, narrow source reads, sequential checkpoints, and only the context needed for each stage. Do not claim a subscription allowance, cost, or usage outcome that has not been verified.

## Traceability and verification levels

Maintain `User Story → spec/US-XX.md → applicable approved ADRs → approved design (when requested) → implementation → stable test case IDs → reports/qa/US-XX-qa-report.md → reviews/US-XX-review.md → finding resolution evidence → human approval`. Reference repository paths and actual evidence. Reuse approved ADRs when they cover the story. Story reports cover the current story only. Complete quote-flow and cross-country verification are project-level checks before final delivery, not prerequisites for each story when later stories are pending.

## Retrospective

### How would this flow change for a five-developer team?
Assign a human owner to each story and a maintainer to the shared form, plan, and terms contracts. Run independent work in parallel once its spec and ADRs are approved. For example, QA can prepare country fixtures while implementation proceeds, while changes to shared contracts need coordinated review before dependent work lands. Use a shared review queue and automated unit, CMS integration, and two-country browser checks so every reviewer sees the same evidence before handoff.

### What did not work as expected, and what changed?
US-01 independent QA hit a model usage limit before the report was ready. The owner chose to retry the original QA agent using existing evidence, and that agent resumed without a model substitution. In US-03, the Angular development server returned its SPA fallback for API requests expected to return 404. QA moved the full browser suite to the static Compose deployment, where the route assertions passed. These incidents showed where to retain verified partial results and where to run checks against the delivery environment.

### Where did we deliberately avoid using AI, and why?
The owner made the specification, architecture, design, and final acceptance decisions. For example, the owner requested removal of the wizard header country controls and accepted the terminal quote revision after manual verification. The owner also authorized Git operations separately. These decisions established business intent, accepted implementation trade-offs, and controlled repository changes. Agents prepared and verified the supporting artifacts.
